title: EDiR Practice Set 6 · abdomen, chest and safety
subtitle: Radform original · abbreviated EDiR-style practice · English
disclaimer: Simulacro original de Radform basado en la estructura publicada del EDiR. No contiene preguntas oficiales ni bancos de pago.

questions.question: Which CT findings support acute mesenteric ischaemia? Choose all that apply.
options: Portal venous gas in advanced disease
questions.explanation: Vascular occlusion together with bowel-wall perfusion abnormalities and gas patterns increases diagnostic confidence.

questions.question: Which HRCT findings are typical of UIP? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: Typical UIP favours basal/subpleural fibrosis with traction bronchiectasis and honeycombing.

questions.question: Acute intraparenchymal haemorrhage on non-contrast CT is usually:
questions.explanation: Fresh blood is generally hyperdense relative to brain parenchyma.

questions.question: Pancreatic necrosis in acute pancreatitis is indicated by:
questions.explanation: Non-enhancement indicates loss of pancreatic perfusion and necrosis.

questions.question: Which CTPA findings may indicate right-heart strain in acute pulmonary embolism? Choose all that apply.
options: Contrast reflux into the IVC/hepatic veins
questions.explanation: These are recognised imaging markers of right ventricular pressure overload.

questions.question: Collimation in ionising-radiation imaging:
options: Has no effect on image quality
questions.explanation: Limiting the field to the anatomy of interest is a core dose-optimisation principle.

questions.question: In a high-risk cirrhotic patient, a lesion with non-rim arterial hyperenhancement and washout:
options: May satisfy imaging criteria for HCC under an appropriate system
questions.explanation: In an appropriate at-risk population this enhancement pattern is characteristic of HCC.

questions.question: Gadolinium administration requires particular consideration in:
options: Advanced renal impairment, depending on agent and clinical context
questions.explanation: Renal function and the gadolinium agent influence risk assessment in advanced kidney disease.

cases.title: Right lower quadrant pain
cases.stem: CT demonstrates an enlarged appendix with mural enhancement and surrounding inflammatory fat stranding.

questions.question: What is the diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The CT appearance is typical of acute appendicitis.

questions.question: Which finding would indicate complicated appendicitis?
options: Extraluminal gas or a periappendiceal abscess
questions.explanation: Perforation may produce extraluminal gas, phlegmon or abscess formation.

cases.title: Sudden pleuritic pain
cases.stem: Chest radiography demonstrates a visceral pleural line with absent lung markings peripheral to it.

questions.question: What is the diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The visceral pleural line and absent peripheral markings identify a pneumothorax.

questions.question: Which feature would increase urgency?
options: A large pneumothorax with mediastinal shift and clinical compromise
questions.explanation: Large size plus tension features or physiological compromise requires urgent management.

cases.title: Acute mesenteric ischaemia
cases.stem: An elderly patient with atrial fibrillation has abrupt severe abdominal pain and elevated lactate. CTA is performed.

questions.question: A proximal embolic defect in the superior mesenteric artery indicates:
questions.explanation: SMA embolism is a major cause of acute mesenteric ischaemia.

questions.question: Absent bowel-wall enhancement and pneumatosis should:
questions.explanation: Loss of enhancement and pneumatosis are serious signs in the appropriate context.

questions.question: Which reporting behaviour would be potentially unsafe?
options: Failing to communicate the arterial occlusion and bowel-ischaemia signs
questions.explanation: Delay in diagnosis can result in bowel necrosis and death.

cases.title: Central lung mass and haemoptysis
cases.stem: A smoker with haemoptysis has a central lung mass causing lobar collapse and enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes.

questions.question: What is the primary diagnostic concern?
questions.explanation: A central obstructing mass with nodal disease in a smoker is highly suspicious for lung cancer.

questions.question: Which information should the report include?
options: Tumour size/location, bronchovascular relationships, nodal disease and visible metastases
questions.explanation: Structured staging-relevant information guides bronchoscopy, biopsy and treatment planning.

questions.question: Which omission would be potentially unsafe?
options: Failing to mention major central airway obstruction or obvious vascular invasion
questions.explanation: Critical airway or vascular involvement may directly alter immediate management and procedural risk.
